We begin, as is our custom, with what Allah the Exalted has made easy of the Book of Allah, and we have finished Surah An-Naba' up to the end of Al-Mutaffifin.

Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. ﴿When the sky is split open﴾ [al-Inshiqaq 1]. The discussion of the basmala (the phrase "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful") has already preceded, and we explained that the basmala is a verse of the Book of Allah set apart, not part of the surah before it or the surah after it. It is recited at the beginning of surahs except Surah Bara'ah (At-Tawbah). It is not a verse of Al-Fatihah (the Opening), although what is found in the mushafs is that it is a verse. The preponderant view, which is the position of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah have mercy on him, and that of the majority of his companions, is that it is not a verse of Al-Fatihah. This is what the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, indicates, where the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, relating from Allah: "I have divided the prayer between Myself and My servant into two halves. When he says: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾, He says: 'My servant has praised Me.' When he says: ﴿The Most Gracious, the Most Merciful﴾, He says: 'My servant has extolled Me.' When he says: ﴿Sovereign of the Day of Recompense﴾, He says: 'My servant has glorified Me.' When he says: ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾, He says: 'This is between Me and My servant in two halves, and My servant shall have what he asks.' When he says: ﴿Guide us to the straight path, the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour, not of those who have earned anger nor of those who are astray﴾, He says: 'This is for My servant, and My servant shall have what he asks.'"[[Muslim (395/38) narrated from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Allah the Exalted said: I have divided the prayer between Me and My servant into two halves, and My servant shall have what he asks. When the servant says: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾, Allah the Exalted says: My servant has praised Me. When he says: ﴿The Most Gracious, the Most Merciful﴾, Allah the Exalted says: My servant has extolled Me. When he says: ﴿Sovereign of the Day of Recompense﴾, He says: My servant has glorified Me; and on one occasion He said: My servant has entrusted Me. When he says: ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾, He says: This is between Me and My servant, and My servant shall have what he asks. When he says: ﴿Guide us to the straight path, the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour, not of those who have earned anger nor of those who are astray﴾, He says: This is for My servant, and My servant shall have what he asks."]].

On this basis, the first verse is ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾, the second is ﴿The Most Gracious, the Most Merciful﴾, the third is ﴿Sovereign of the Day of Recompense﴾, the fourth is ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾, the fifth is ﴿Guide us to the straight path﴾, the sixth is ﴿the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour﴾, and the seventh is ﴿not of those who have earned anger nor of those who are astray﴾.

This view, just as it agrees with what the Sunnah indicates, also agrees with the surah in wording and meaning. In wording: the first three verses all belong to the right of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and the last three verses all belong to the right of the human being: ﴿Guide us to the straight path (6), the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour, not of those who have earned anger nor of those who are astray﴾, all of which belong to the right of the human being. The fourth verse, the middle one, lies between Allah and the servant. This is the preponderant view regarding Al-Fatihah, that it has seven verses, the first of which is ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾.

As for the surah we begin now, it is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿When the sky is split open﴾. ﴿Split open﴾ means opened and cleft apart, like His saying: ﴿And when the sky is opened﴾ [al-Mursalat 9], and His saying: ﴿And when the sky splits open and becomes red like melted oil (37). So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny? (38). On that Day, neither man nor jinn will be asked about his sin﴾ [ar-Rahman 37–39]. Thus its splitting is on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿When the sky is split open﴾.

﴿ ﴾

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 84, verse 2:

﴿And it hearkens to its Lord and it is right that it should⦆ [al-Inshiqaq: 2] ﴿Adhinat﴾ means it listened and obeyed. Its Lord, mighty and majestic is He, commanded it to split open, so it split open, whereas it had been, as Allah the Most High described it, ﴿seven firm (heavens)﴾ [an-Naba': 12], strong, as the Most High said: ﴿And the heaven We constructed with might﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 47], meaning with strength. So this strong, mighty heaven will split open on the Day of Resurrection; it will be cleft and rent asunder, by the permission of Allah, glorified and exalted is He.

﴿And it hearkens to its Lord and it is right that it should﴾ means: it is right for it to hearken, that is, to listen and obey. For who commanded it? Its Lord commanded it, its Creator, mighty and majestic is He, so it listens and obeys, just as it listened and obeyed at the beginning of its creation. At the beginning of its creation, Allah, blessed and exalted is He, said: ﴿Then He turned to the heaven when it was smoke and said to it and to the earth: "Come both of you, willingly or unwillingly." They said: "We come willingly, obedient."﴾ [Fussilat: 11]. So reflect, O human being, weak mortal, on how these great creatures listened and obeyed Allah, mighty and majestic is He, with this great obedience at the beginning of creation and at its end! At the beginning of creation He said: ﴿Come both of you, willingly or unwillingly. They said: We come willingly, obedient﴾; at the end of creation: ﴿When the heaven splits asunder (1) and hearkens to its Lord and it is right that it should⦆ [al-Inshiqaq: 1-2], it is right for it to hearken; it listens and obeys.

Then he repeated, saying: ﴿And it hearkens to its Lord and it is right that it should⦆ [al-Inshiqaq: 5], as an emphasis on its listening to its Lord and its obedience to its Lord.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 84, verse 3:

﴿And when the earth is stretched out﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 3]. This earth on which we now live is not stretched out. Firstly, it is a rounded sphere (kurah mudawwarah), although its northern and southern sides are slightly open, i.e., slightly extended; so it is round now.

Then, it is also uneven: in it are the very high and the very low, in it are valleys, in it are plains, in it are sands, so it is not level. But on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿when the earth is stretched out﴾, i.e., it will be stretched out in one extension like the stretching of a hide (adim), meaning like the stretching of a skin, as if it were spread out as a carpet or a sheet (samat). It will be stretched out, so that those upon it, who are the creation, will be made to hear the caller and will be within the sight of the eye. But now this is not possible; the eye does not reach them. If people were spread out on the earth, you would find the distant ones low, and you would not see them. But on the Day of Resurrection, when it is stretched out, its farthest point becomes like its nearest point, as came in the hadith: "The caller will make them hear, and the sight will reach them all"[[Agreed upon (muttafaq 'alayh); al-Bukhari (4712) and Muslim (194 / 327), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him).]].

﴿

﴾﴿﴾﴿﴿وَإِذَا الْأَرْضُ مُدَّتْ﴾ ﴿وَأَلْقَتْ مَا فِيهَا وَتَخَلَّتْ﴾ ﴿وَأَذِنَتْ لِرَبِّهَا وَحُقَّتْ﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 3-5].

﴿أَلْقَتْ مَا فِيهَا﴾ "It casts out what is in it." What is in it? In it are the corpses of the children of Adam, which it will cast out on the Day of Resurrection. These corpses will be cast out, and people will come out of their graves to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, just as He originated them at the first creation. That is, just as they came out of their mothers' wombs, they will come out of the bowels of the earth. Did you come out of your mother's womb barefoot or shod? Answer me.

* Students: Barefoot.

* The Shaykh: Clothed or naked? Naked. Circumcised or uncircumcised (aghral)? Uncircumcised. However, some people are born circumcised, but most people come out of their mothers' wombs uncircumcised (ghurlan). Likewise, you will come out of the bowels of the earth on the Day of Resurrection barefoot, with no sandals on you, naked, with no clothing on you, and uncircumcised, not circumcised. When the Prophet (ﷺ) related this, 'Aisha said: "O Messenger of Allah, the men and the women?!"

He said: "The men and the women."

She said: "Their private parts exposed?!"

He said: "Yes, but the matter is too grave for that to concern them."[[Al-Bukhari (6527) and Muslim (2859/56) narrated from 'Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) that she said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection barefoot, naked and uncircumcised." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, the men and the women together, looking at one another!" He (ﷺ) said: "O 'Aisha, the matter is too severe for them to look at one another."]]

The matter is severe. Every person is preoccupied with himself: ﴿لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مِنْهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ شَأْنٌ يُغْنِيهِ﴾ ["Every one of them, that Day, will have a matter that occupies him."] [Abasa: 37].

When a person imagines the people at that time, even merely imagining it, he trembles and fears. If he is intelligent and a believer, he will work for that Day. For this reason Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿ ﴾

﴿And when the earth is stretched out (3), and casts out what is within it and empties itself (4), and hearkens to its Lord, and it is fitting that it should [5].﴾ [Al-Inshiqaq: 3-5]. ﴿أَذِنَتْ﴾ means that it listened and obeyed its Lord, and ﴿وَحُقَّتْ﴾ [it is fitting]. Having previously been rounded, with high and low places in it, it became like a hide (جِلد), stretched out in one single extension.

Then the Most High said: ﴿O mankind, indeed you are laboring toward your Lord with labor, and you will meet Him﴾ [al-Inshiqaq 6]. Al-kadih is one who strives with diligence and a kind of hardship. His saying ﴿toward your Lord﴾ means that you labor with a labor that brings you to your Lord, a labor that leads to Allah. That is, whatever your labor is, its ultimate end is to whom? To Allah, because we will all die, and when we die we return to Allah the Mighty and Majestic. Whatever you do, the final destination is Allah the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And that to your Lord is the finality﴾ [al-Najm 42]. For this reason He said: ﴿laboring toward your Lord with labor﴾. Even the disobedient one is laboring, and his goal is Allah the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Indeed, to Us is their return. Then indeed, upon Us is their account﴾ [al-Ghashiyah 25-26].

However, the difference between the obedient and the disobedient is that the obedient one does a deed that Allah is pleased with, which brings him to the pleasure of Allah on the Day of Resurrection, while the disobedient one does a deed that angers Allah. Yet, despite that, where does he end? To Allah the Mighty and Majestic. Therefore His saying ﴿O mankind﴾ includes every human being, believer and disbeliever.

﴿Indeed, you are laboring toward your Lord with labor, and you will meet Him﴾. The grammarians say that the fa' (فَ) indicates sequence and immediacy, meaning: so you will meet Him. From a distance or from nearness? From nearness: ﴿Indeed, what you are promised is coming﴾ [al-An'am 134], and everything that is coming is near: ﴿And what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near﴾ [al-Shura 17].

If you want it to become clear to you that meeting the Lord the Mighty and Majestic is near, then look at what has passed of your life so far. If a hundred years have passed, this year is, as it were, what? One hour. All that has passed of our lives is as if it were one hour. Therefore it is near. Then, when a person dies, do you think that the barzakh (the intermediate state) between the life of this world and the Hereafter is long? It is near, like a moment. When a person sleeps a peaceful sleep, let us say he slept for twenty-four hours and then got up, how much does that sleep amount to?

* A student: A minute.

* The Shaykh: One minute, although he may have slept twenty-four hours. If this is the case while the soul is still in the body, time passes at this speed, then what about when the soul, after leaving the body, is occupied either with bliss or with punishment? Millions of years will pass over the person while it is as if they were nothing, because the extension of time in our waking state is not like the extension of time in our sleeping state, is it not? You agree with this. That is, a person awake from sunrise to midday feels that the time is long, but if he were asleep, it would be as if it were nothing.

He whom Allah caused to die for a hundred years and then resurrected: ﴿He said: How long have you remained? He said: I have remained a day or part of a day﴾ [al-Baqarah 259], a hundred years. The People of the Cave remained in their cave three hundred and nine years. When they were raised, some of them said to others: How long have you remained? They said: ﴿We have remained a day or part of a day﴾ [al-Kahf 19]. This indicates that people... that is, a person wonders: how do millions of years pass over these dead? We say: yes, these are millions of years, but it is as if it were only one minute. That is, the state of a person after his soul departs from his body, whether the departure is complete or partial, is other than his state when the soul is in the body. When the soul is in the body, it suffers hardship, troubles, anxieties and whisperings, things that make time long for him. But in sleep time contracts greatly, and in death it contracts even more. So those who have died, for them millions or thousands of years are as if they had not died except today. If they were resurrected, it would be said to them: How long have you remained? They would say: We have remained a day or part of a day.

This is a matter about which a person may have a doubt, but there is no difficulty in the matter. However long the period is for the people of the graves, it is short. For this reason He said: ﴿So you will meet Him﴾, using the fa' that indicates what? Sequence and immediacy. How quickly you will meet Allah the Mighty and Majestic.

Then Allah the Mighty and Majestic divided people at the time of meeting Allah the Most High into two categories: among them are those who take their book in their right hand, and I ask Allah to make me and you among them, and among them are those who take their book from behind their back.

If Allah the Most High wills, the discussion of that will come in the next session.

The Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on Surah 84, verses 7–9:

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿As for him who is given his record in his right hand, (7) he will be called to a easy account﴾ [al-Inshiqaq 7, 8].

When He mentioned that the servant, indeed the human being, every human being, is toiling (kadih) toward his Lord, (kadih) meaning: laboring with diligence and energy, (toward his Lord) meaning that this labor of his ends with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And to Allah belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and to Him the whole matter will be returned﴾ [Hud 123]. When He mentioned this, He said: ﴿As for him who is given his record in his right hand﴾, indicating that among these laborers are those who are given their record in their right hand, and among them are those who are given their record from behind their backs.

﴿As for him who is given his record in his right hand﴾: here ﴿given﴾ (utiya) is a verb in the passive voice, with the agent unnamed. So who is it that gives him? It may be the angels or other than them; we do not know. The important point is that he is given his record in his right hand, he receives it with his right hand.

﴿He will be called to an easy account﴾ [al-Inshiqaq 8] meaning: Allah, exalted is He, will reckon with him by counting his deeds against him, but it is an easy reckoning, with no hardship in it at all. As the Sunnah has come to affirm, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will be alone with His believing servant and will make him acknowledge his sins, saying: "You did such-and-such, you did such-and-such, you did such-and-such," and he will acknowledge it and not deny it. Then Allah, exalted is He, says: "I concealed them for you in the world, and I forgive them for you today."[[Al-Bukhari (2441) and Muslim (2768/52) narrate from Ibn 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) that a man asked him: "How did you hear the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) speak about the private conference (najwa)?" He said: "I heard him say: 'The believer will be brought near on the Day of Resurrection to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, until He places His covering (kanaf) over him, and makes him acknowledge his sins, saying: Do you recognize (such-and-such)? He will say: My Lord, I recognize it. He will say: Indeed I concealed them for you in the world, and I forgive them for you today. Then his record of good deeds will be given to him. As for the disbelievers and the hypocrites, they will be called out before the heads of all creation: These are the ones who lied against Allah.'"]] There is no doubt that this is an easy reckoning, in which the favor of Allah upon the servant appears, along with His joy in him and his rejoicing.

﴿He will be called to an easy account﴾: the one who reckons with him is Allah, Mighty and Majestic, as He said: ﴿Indeed, to Us is their return (25), then indeed upon Us is their reckoning﴾ [al-Ghashiyah 25, 26].

﴿He will be called to an easy account (8) and will return to his family joyful﴾ [al-Inshiqaq 8, 9]: he returns from the reckoning to his family in Paradise, joyful, meaning joyful of heart. The Prophet (ﷺ) informed that "The first group to enter Paradise will be in the form of the moon on the night of the full moon,"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3246) and Muslim (2834/14), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him).]] then after that they will be in ranks, and this indicates joy of heart, because when the heart is delighted, the face is illuminated.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 84, verse 10:

﴿But as for him who is given his record behind his back (10), he will call for destruction (11) and will burn in a Blaze (12).﴾ These are the wretched, may Allah protect us. His record is given to him behind his back, not in his right hand. In the other verse, in Surah al-Haqqah, ﴿But as for him who is given his record in his left hand﴾ [al-Haqqah: 25], it has been said that whoever is not given his record in his right hand is divided into two categories: some are given their record in the left hand, and others are given their record behind their back. The closer view, and Allah knows best, is that he is given his record in the left hand, but his hand is turned around so that it ends up behind his back, as a sign that he cast the Book of Allah behind his back, and the taking with the left hand is then followed by the hand being twisted backward, as a sign that he has turned his back on the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, paid it no heed, did not lift his head toward it, and saw no harm in opposing it.

Qur'an 84:11: "Then he will call for destruction."

That is, he will call down destruction upon himself, meaning he will call out for ruin (thubur) upon himself. He will say: "Woe to me! Alas, my destruction!" and whatever is similar to such words of regret and anguish. But this will not benefit him on that Day, because the time for action has ended. The time for action is in this world; as for the Hereafter, there is no action, only recompense.

﴿So he will call for destruction, and he will burn in a blazing fire﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 11, 12]. That is: he will enter the Fire that is kindled for him, and he will be in it forever, because he was a disbeliever, we seek refuge with Allah.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 84, verse 13:

﴿Indeed, he used to be joyful among his family.﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 13] He was joyful among his family in the worldly life; but this joy was followed by regret and constant, enduring sorrow. Connect His statement, exalted is He, concerning the one who is given his record in his right hand: ﴿He will return to his family joyful﴾, and this one—may Allah protect us—﴿used to be joyful among his family﴾. You will see the difference between the two joys: the first joy is a lasting joy, we ask Allah to make us and you among its people, and the second joy is a passing joy, it has gone; ﴿used to be joyful among his family﴾. As for now, there is no joy for him.

Indeed, he thought that he would never return. ﴿He thought that he would never return﴾: that he would not come back after death. For this reason they used to deny the resurrection and say, "There is no resurrection," and they would say: ﴿Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?﴾

Qur'anic quotations: ﴿Indeed, he thought that he would never return.﴾ Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Yes!﴾ That is, he will return and come back. ﴿Indeed, his Lord was ever Seeing of him.﴾ [Al-Inshiqaq 15] Meaning: he will return to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, who is Seeing of his deeds, and He will call him to account for them in accordance with what His wisdom and justice require.

(...) Thursday. With it we conclude what remains of Surat al-Inshiqaq. We have reached His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿So I swear by the twilight glow, (16) and by the night and what it gathers, (17) and by the moon when it becomes full, (18) that you will surely travel from stage to stage.﴾ [al-Inshiqaq 16-19]. This sentence consists of an oath, the one sworn by, the thing sworn to, and the one swearing. In His words ﴿la uqsimu bi-l-shafaq﴾ (I swear by the twilight), someone may think that the meaning of ﴿la uqsimu﴾ is negation, but it is not so. Rather, it is affirmation. The particle "la" here is brought for emphasis (tanbih). If it were removed in other than the Qur'an, the speech would still be sound. Similar examples are: ﴿la uqsimu bi-hadha al-balad﴾ (I swear by this city) [al-Balad 1], ﴿la uqsimu bi-yawm al-qiyamah﴾ (I swear by the Day of Resurrection) [al-Qiyamah 1], ﴿fa-la uqsimu bi-rabb al-mashariq﴾ (so I swear by the Lord of the easts) [al-Ma'arij 40], and ﴿fa-la uqsimu bi-ma tubsirun﴾ (so I swear by what you see) [al-Haqqah 38]. The scholars all say that "la" in these is for emphasis, and that the oath is affirmative.

As for the one swearing, it is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. He, glory be to Him, is the one who swears. As for the thing sworn by in this verse, it is the twilight and what is conjoined to it.

If someone asks: why does Allah swear to His own report, while He, glory be to Him, is the Truthful even without an oath? Likewise, the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him and his family, swears to his report while he is truthful without an oath?

We say: an oath reinforces speech. The Arabic Qur'an was revealed in the Arabic tongue. Since it is their custom to reinforce speech with oaths, this style became current in the Arabic tongue in which the Qur'an was revealed.

As for His words ﴿bi-l-shafaq﴾ (by the twilight glow): al-shafaq is the redness that appears after the sunset. When this redness disappears, the time of Maghrib (sunset prayer) ends and the time of 'Isha' (night prayer) begins. This is the view of most scholars. Some of them said: it is when the whiteness disappears, and it disappears about half an hour after the redness. However, what the majority hold, and it is said that Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, returned to it, is that al-shafaq is the redness. When this shafaq disappears, the time of 'Isha' begins and the time of Maghrib ends.

﴿Wa-l-layli wa-ma wasaq﴾ (and by the night and what it gathers): this is also a thing sworn by, conjoined to al-shafaq. That is: "And I swear by the night and what it gathers." These are two oaths: the night, and what it gathers. The night is well known, so what is the meaning of ﴿ma wasaq﴾? That is, what it gathers, because the night gathers wild animals, insects, and the like. They gather and come out; they emerge from their dens and houses. Likewise, it may also point to the gathering of people with one another.

﴿Wa-l-qamari idha ittasaq﴾ (and by the moon when it becomes full): the moon is well known. The meaning of ﴿idha ittasaq﴾ is: when its light gathers and is complete and perfected, and that is on the nights of full moon. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, swore by the night and what it gathers, that is, what it gathers, and by the moon, because it is the sign of the night.

Then He said after that: ﴿la-tarkabunna tabaqan 'an tabaq﴾ (you will surely travel from stage to stage). The address here is to all people. That is: you will surely pass from state to state. This means that conditions change. So it includes states of time, states of place, states of bodies, and states of hearts. Pay attention: it contains four things. ﴿la-tarkabunna tabaqan 'an tabaq﴾, what did we say about it? State after state. So what are they? We said: states of time, states of place, states of bodies, and states of hearts.

We know that the states of time change: ﴿wa-tilka al-ayyamu nudawiluha bayna al-nas﴾ (and these days We alternate among people) [Al 'Imran 140]. So there is a day in which there is joy, expansion, and relaxation of the soul, and another day which is the opposite, even to the point that a person feels this without there being any known cause. On this the poet says:

A day for us and a day against us,
and a day we are troubled, and a day we are made happy.

This is something each one of us knows in himself: you wake up today feeling companionable, joyful, and happy; the next day, the opposite, without a reason. But thus it must be that a person travels from stage to stage.

Likewise with places: a person stays in one place this day, and the next day in another place, and a third, and a fourth, until his stations end in the Hereafter. Before the Hereafter, there are the graves, which are temporary stations. The graves are not the final stations; rather they are a stage. A Bedouin heard a man recite the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿alhakumu al-takathur (1) hatta zurtumu al-maqabir﴾ (Rivalry in worldly increase distracts you until you visit the graves) [al-Takathur 1-2]. The Bedouin said: "By Allah, the visitor does not remain." The Bedouin, by his innate nature, understood that beyond these graves there is something to which the final destination leads, because, as we know, the visitor visits and then moves on. By this we know that what we hear in the newspapers, "So-and-so has passed away, then they carried him to his final resting place," is a great error, and its implication is disbelief in the Last Day. Because if you make the grave the final resting place, this means there is nothing after it, and this is disbelief. Whoever holds that the grave is the final resting place with nothing after it is a disbeliever. The final resting place is either Paradise or Fire.

We have now mentioned two states: the first is time, and the second is place.

The third is bodies. A person travels through bodies from stage to stage. Listen to the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Allahu alladhi khalaqakum min da'fin thumma ja'ala min ba'di da'fin quwwatan thumma ja'ala min ba'di quwwatin da'fan wa-shaybatan yakhluqu ma yasha'u wa-huwa al-'alimu al-qadir﴾ (It is Allah who created you from weakness, then made after weakness strength, then made after strength weakness and gray hair. He creates what He wills, and He is the All-Knowing, the All-Powerful) [al-Rum 54]. A human is first created as a small child. You can gather his hands and feet in one of your hands and carry him with that hand, weak. Then he keeps growing stronger little by little until he becomes a young man, robust and strong. Then, when he reaches full strength, he returns to weakness.

Some scholars have compared the state of the body to the state of the moon: it appears as a weak crescent, then grows little by little until it is filled with light, then returns, diminishing little by little until it vanishes. We ask Allah to grant us and you a good ending. This is the state of bodies.

The fourth: the state of hearts. And what can make you know what the states of hearts are! The states of hearts are trial, calamity, blessing, and affliction. The hearts of all the children of Adam are between two fingers of the Most Merciful; He turns them however He wills. If He wills, He causes them to deviate, and if He wills, He guides them, every heart. When the Prophet, peace be upon him, related this hadith, he said: "O Turner of the hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion."[[Narrated by Ahmad (26576) from the hadith of Umm Salamah, may Allah be pleased with her.]] So hearts have wondrous states. At times the heart is attached to the world, and at times it is attached to something of the world. At times it is attached to wealth, and wealth is its greatest concern. At times it is attached to women, and women are its greatest concern. At times it is attached to palaces and houses, and that is its greatest concern. At times it is attached to vehicles and cars, and that is its greatest concern. At times it is with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: always with Allah, attached to Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, and it sees that the whole world is a means to worship Allah and obey Allah. It uses the world, because the world was created for it, and the world does not use it.

Look, my brothers: do you think the people of the world are served by the world, or do they serve it? It is they who serve it. They are the ones who exhaust themselves in acquiring it. But the people of the Hereafter are the ones who use the world, and the world serves them. Therefore they take from it only in the way of Allah's pleasure, and they spend it only in Allah's pleasure, the Mighty and Majestic. They use it in taking and spending. But the people of the world, who exhaust themselves with it, stay up through the nights reviewing ledgers, reviewing checks, reviewing expenses, reviewing payments, reviewing what they took and what they spent. These, in reality, are used by the world, and they do not use it. But the man at peace, whose provision Allah has made sufficient, by which he is independent of people and is not occupied by it from obedience to Allah, this is the one the world serves. These are the states of hearts.

The states of hearts are the greatest of the four states. Therefore it is incumbent upon all of us, and I say it to myself before you, to review our hearts every hour, every moment: Where have you turned, O heart? Where have you gone? Why do you turn away from Allah? Why do you look right and left? But we seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Satan runs through the son of Adam like the blood runs, and he has overcome many people, to the point that he turns a person away from his prayer, which is the head of his capital after the two testimonies. You find that when he enters his prayer, his heart goes right and left until he exits his prayer, and he has understood nothing of it. And people cry out, saying: "Our prayer does not forbid us from indecency and wrongdoing. Where is Allah's promise?!"

It is said: O my brother, is your prayer a prayer?! If, from the moment you say "Allahu akbar," the doorways of endless whisperings open for you, are you then one who prays?! You prayed with your body, but you did not pray with your heart. And it has come in the hadith from the Prophet, peace be upon him: "You will only have from your prayer what you understood of it,"[[It is a report from the saying of 'Ammar ibn Yasir, may Allah be pleased with him, mentioned by Abu Talib al-Makki in Qut al-Qulub (2/170) with the wording: "Only what one understands of his prayer is written for the servant." Ibn al-Mubarak narrated in al-Zuhd (1300) from 'Ammar, may Allah be pleased with him, his saying: "Nothing of a man's prayer is written for him of what he forgot."]] half of it, a quarter of it, a third of it, a tenth of it, a fifth of it, according to what you understand of it. So hearts travel from stage to stage.

This is something each one of us knows in himself: you wake up today feeling companionable, joyful, and happy; the next day, the opposite, without a reason. But thus it must be that a person travels from stage to stage.

And what harm would befall them if they believed?!

And if he is a liar, then upon him is his lying; but if he is truthful, some of what he promises you will afflict you.﴾ [Ghafir 28] So what is there for a person to lose if he believes?! Therefore He said, rebuking them: ﴿So what is wrong with them that they do not believe?﴾

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 84, verse 21:

﴿And when the Qur'an is recited to them, they do not prostrate.﴾ That is: they do not submit to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Prostration here means submission to Allah, even if you do not prostrate upon the ground; rather, your heart prostrates to Allah in humility and submission when you hear His verses.

Test yourself, my brother: when the Qur'an is recited to you, does your heart prostrate, soften, and become humbled? If this is so, then you are among the believers; ﴿When His verses are recited to them, they increase them in faith﴾ [al-Anfal 2]. But if your heart is not like this, then there is in you a resemblance to the polytheists, of whom it is said: when the Qur'an is recited to them, they do not prostrate.

Among the signs of submission to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when reciting the Qur'an, is that a person, when he recites a verse of prostration, prostrates to Allah, humbling himself and submitting to Him. Some scholars have used this verse as evidence for the obligation of prostration, i.e., the prostration of recitation, and said: whoever passes by a verse of prostration and does not prostrate is sinful.

The correct view is that it is not obligatory, although this position, namely the view of obligation, is the doctrine of Abu Hanifah and the preference of Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him. But this is a weak opinion (marjuh), because it is established in the Sahih, from the Commander of the Faithful 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, that "he once delivered a sermon to the people and recited Surat an-Nahl, and when he reached the verse of prostration, he came down from the pulpit and prostrated. Then he recited it on the second Friday, and passed by it without prostrating, and he, may Allah be pleased with him, said: Indeed Allah has not prescribed prostration upon us except if we wish."[[Al-Bukhari (1077) narrated from Rabi'ah ibn 'Abdullah ibn al-Hudayr al-Taymi that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, recited on the pulpit on Friday Surat an-Nahl, until when he reached the prostration he came down and prostrated, and the people prostrated. And 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, did not prostrate.]] This took place in the presence of the Companions, and no one objected to it, and his Sunnah, may Allah be pleased with him, is among the Sunnahs we have been commanded to follow. On this basis, the preponderant view is that the prostration of recitation is not obligatory, but it is a strongly emphasized Sunnah. So when you pass by a verse of prostration, prostrate at whatever time you are: in the morning, in the evening, at night, or during the day; you say "Allahu Akbar" when prostrating, and when you rise you do not say "Allahu Akbar" nor give the salam. This applies when you prostrate outside the prayer. As for if you prostrate during the prayer, then you must say "Allahu Akbar" when you prostrate and say "Allahu Akbar" when you rise, because when it occurs within the prayer it has the ruling of prostration within the prayer.

Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Rather, those who disbelieve deny. And Allah is most knowing of what they conceal﴾ [al-Inshiqaq 22, 23].

We will limit ourselves to this, because the remaining time is for questions, and the rest of the surah, although we had promised you to complete it, will be in the next session, God willing.

Translation:

In this session we will speak about the end of Surah al-Inshiqaq, which is the words of the Blessed and Exalted: ﴿Nay, those who disbelieve deny. And Allah is most knowing of what they conceal. So give them tidings of a painful punishment, except those who believe and do righteous deeds; for them is a reward never to be cut off.﴾ [al-Inshiqaq 22–25].

When the Exalted mentioned that when the Qur'an is recited to them they do not prostrate, He made clear that the cause of their abandoning prostration is their denial of what the messengers, upon them be prayers and peace, brought. For everyone whose faith is true must comply with the command and avoid the prohibition, because true faith compels its possessor to do so. You will not find a person who violates the sacred prohibitions or leaves the obligations except because of the weakness of his faith. For this reason, faith according to the people of the Sunnah and the Jama'ah (Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah, the adherents of the prophetic way and the main body of the community) is affirmation that necessarily entails acceptance and submission. So whenever you see a man abandoning the obligations, or some of them, or committing the forbidden acts, know that his faith is weak; for if his faith were strong, he would not neglect the obligations nor violate the prohibitions. Therefore He said here: ﴿Nay, those who disbelieve deny﴾, meaning: in their abandoning prostration, this was due to their denial of what the messengers brought.

Qur'anic quotation: ﴿And Allah is most knowing of what they conceal﴾ — the verb يوعون (yūʿūn) means "they gather and store up" (from the root و-ع-ي, to collect and keep in a vessel).

That is, He, glory be to Him and exalted is He, is most knowing of what they gather up; that is, of what they gather within their breasts, what they accumulate of their wealth, and what they unite upon of opposition to the Messengers, of hostility toward the Messengers, indeed of waging war against the Messengers and fighting them. You know that the disbelievers have been enemies of the Messengers since the time Allah sent the Messengers, upon them be prayers and peace, and that they gather against them and plot against them. So Allah the Exalted threatens them in this verse: ﴿And Allah is most knowing of what they gather up﴾; that is, of what they gather of words, deeds, rancours, enmities and wealth directed against the Messengers, upon them be prayers and peace.

Then He said: ﴿So give them tidings of a painful punishment.﴾ Inform them of the painful punishment that must come to pass. The address in His words ﴿So give them tidings﴾ is general, directed to the Messenger (ﷺ) and to everyone who is fit to be addressed; whoever is fit to be addressed is included in this. And it is incumbent upon us to give every disbeliever tidings of a painful punishment: we give every disbeliever tidings of a painful punishment awaiting him, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And wait, for they too are waiting.﴾ [As-Sajdah 30]

Then He said: "Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds; for them is a reward never to be cut off." (Qur'an 84:25)

"Illa" (except) here carries the meaning of "lakin" (but), and it cannot be a connected exception (istithna' muttasil), because those who believe are not among the deniers in any way; rather, they are believers who affirm the truth. This is the disconnected exception (istithna' munqati'), i.e., if the excepted item is not of the same kind as the item excepted from, then it is a disconnected exception, and "illa" is taken to mean "lakin." That is: "But those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is a reward never to be cut off."

Those who believe in their hearts, and whose belief necessitates their performance of righteous deeds: these are the ones for whom there is no punishment, and who do not await punishment. For them is a reward never to be cut off.

If it is asked: What is a righteous deed?

The answer: A righteous deed is that which combines two things:

The first: sincerity to Allah, the Exalted, such that what drives the action is sincerity to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, seeking His pleasure, seeking His reward, seeking deliverance from the Fire. A person does not intend by his deed any worldly thing. For this reason the scholars said: acts which are only performed as worship may not be taken payment for; such as the adhan, for example: it is not valid to call the adhan for a wage; and leading prayer (imamah): it is not valid to lead prayer for a wage; and reciting the Qur'an: it is not valid to recite for a wage. This differs from teaching the Qur'an, which is valid for a wage because it is transitive (muta'addin), and the payment is for the teaching, not for the recitation. But if someone comes and says, "I want to recite the Qur'an for a wage," that is not valid and not permissible; because among the conditions of a righteous deed is that it be sincere to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and whoever recites for a wage or worships for a wage has not made his deed sincere to Allah, so his deed will not be accepted.

As for the second thing, it is that the action be in conformity with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him and his family; that is, that a person follow the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in his action, doing what he did and abstaining from what he abstained from. So whatever the Prophet ﷺ did while its cause existed, the Sunnah is in doing it; meaning, if the cause of a matter existed in the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him and his family, and he did not do it, then the Sunnah is abandoning it.

Therefore we say: what many Muslims do today, or most Muslims today, of celebrating the birthday of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him and his family, on the twelfth day of this month, is a bid'ah (innovation) that has no basis in the Sunnah; because the Messenger of Allah, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him and his family, did not celebrate his birthday, nor did his rightly-guided caliphs. Moreover, we know with certainty that if it were prescribed, the Prophet, peace be upon him, would not have left it without explaining it to the Ummah; for upon him is the conveying (of the message). Since he did not tell the Ummah that this occasion is legislated for celebration, and since he himself did not do it, nor did his rightly-guided caliphs, it is known that it is a bid'ah, and that its doer increases only in distance from Allah. We ask Allah for well-being.

This bid'ah first came into being in the fourth century (AH); that is, more than three hundred years after the Islamic Ummah had passed. They claim that in it they glorify the Messenger of Allah, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him and his family. The reality is that every bid'ah does not contain glorification of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him and his family; for glorifying the Messenger of Allah is only in following his Sunnah, as Allah, the Exalted, said: "O you who believe, do not put yourselves forward before Allah and His Messenger, and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing." [al-Hujurat 1].

Let us look at this bid'ah: does it have a basis in history? Does it have a basis in the Shari'ah?

We say: it has no basis in history; this is because the birth of the Messenger, peace be upon him, is disputed among more than five opinions, after agreement that it was in Rabi' (the third month), but it is disputed: on the first day, on the second day, on the ninth, on the tenth, on the twelfth; there are opinions on it. Some astronomer scholars of this age have preferred that it was on the ninth day and not the twelfth day, so it is invalidated, from the historical standpoint, that it was on the twelfth day.

As for the legal standpoint, it is invalid for several reasons:

First: it is an act of worship that Allah did not legislate, nor did His Messenger, nor the rightly-guided caliphs whose Sunnah we were commanded to follow. If a claimant claims that this is legislated in the Qur'an and Sunnah, or in the practice of the rightly-guided caliphs or the Companions, then the burden of proof is on him; for the burden of proof is upon the claimant. And who is able to do so? He will not find a way to produce a single piece of evidence from the Book, the Sunnah, or the practice of the rightly-guided caliphs or the Companions, that celebrating the birthday of the Messenger, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him and his family, is Sunnah.

Second: we say: this bid'ah is either true or false. If it were true, it would follow that the Prophet, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him and his family, was either ignorant of the truth or knowing of it and concealing it; and both matters are false and utterly impossible: that the Messenger ﷺ be ignorant of some part of the Shari'ah of Allah, or that he know it but not explain it to the Ummah. For the first possibility entails that he was ignorant of the Shari'ah though he is its bearer; and the second possibility entails that he concealed what Allah revealed to him, and far be it from him. Had he concealed what Allah revealed to him, he would have concealed the saying of Allah, the Exalted: "And you were concealing within yourself that which Allah is to disclose, and you feared the people, while Allah has more right that you fear Him." [al-Ahzab 37].

Third: we say: if it becomes clear that it is a bid'ah, then it is not permissible for anyone to establish it; based on the saying of the Prophet, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him and his family: "Beware of newly invented matters, for every newly invented matter is an innovation, every innovation is misguidance, and every misguidance is in the Fire." [[Narrated by Abu Dawud (4607) from the hadith of al-Irbad ibn Sariyah, may Allah be pleased with him, without the phrase "and every misguidance is in the Fire"; that phrase is from another hadith narrated by al-Nasa'i (1578) from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, may Allah be pleased with them both.]] And if the truth were to follow their desires, and everyone who wished to claim that there is legislation in this were to legislate, the Ummah would differ, religion would be torn apart, and every people would have a particular religion; and this is contrary to what the Islamic Shari'ah brought: the obligation of unity upon the word of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him and his family.

Fourth: we say: this bid'ah has not been confined to mere gathering, prayer upon the Prophet ﷺ, mentioning his virtues, his merits, and his Shari'ah; rather, it has departed from this to something else: to panegyric poems extreme in exaggeration to its utmost limit, even going beyond human nature to the rights of the Divine, Mighty and Majestic. These who gather would chant the poem of al-Busiri, in which he addresses the Prophet, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him and his family, saying:

"O most noble of creation, I have none to seek refuge in
Other than you when the grave calamity befalls,
If you do not take my hand on the Day of Return with pardon,
Then say: 'O slip of the foot!'
For indeed from your generosity is the world and its counterpart..." ............................(ضرَّتها) what is it?
* Students: The Hereafter.
* The Shaykh: The Hereafter.

"......................... And from your knowledge is the knowledge of the Preserved Tablet and the Pen."

Some scholars said: if the matter is like this, nothing remains for Allah. And Allah, the Exalted, was no longer the refuge at times of hardship and fear; rather the Messenger, peace be upon him, who possesses for himself no benefit or harm except what Allah wills, became the refuge. This is the utmost of exaggeration which the Messenger, peace be upon him, forbade. Thus these people who claim that they draw near to Allah through such celebrations, and that they are the lovers of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him and his family, have in reality become those who distance themselves from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, by associating with Him what He has not sent down any authority for. And there is no doubt that the Messenger, peace be upon him, would never be pleased with this at all.

If they say: the origin of this is love for the Messenger of Allah, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him and his family, and in order to show the Christians that we care for our Messenger as they cared for theirs by making a festival for his birth:

We say: if you are truthful in love of Allah and His Messenger, then here is the just and fair measure, which is His saying, the Exalted: "Say, if you should love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you." [Ali 'Imran 31]. For this reason, whenever a person is more intense in love of Allah, he is more intense in following the Messenger of Allah, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him and his family; and whenever he is less in love of Allah, he is less in following the Messenger of Allah, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him and his family. So if you see a man who claims love of Allah and His Messenger but does not adhere to the Shari'ah, know that he is a liar; for love of Allah and His Messenger necessarily produces following the Messenger, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him and his family.

The conclusion is that it is obligatory upon the students of knowledge here in Saudi Arabia and in other Islamic lands to explain to the common people and to non-common people that this celebration has no basis in the Sunnah, that it is a bid'ah, and that it only increases a person in distance from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; for it is a legislation in the religion of Allah of what is not part of it.

If someone says: Is not prayer upon the Messenger, peace be upon him, legislated at all times?

The answer: Yes. Increase in prayer upon the Messenger, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him and his family, and Allah will magnify for you a reward through it; and whoever prays upon him once, Allah will pray upon him ten times for it. But arranging it on a specific night, gathering for it, and mentioning panegyrics and extravagant poems exaggerated to the utmost limit of exaggeration: this is what is forbidden.

We do not say: do not pray upon the Messenger; we say: increase in prayer. And we do not say: do not love the Messenger; we say: love the Messenger more than you love yourselves, and your faith is not complete without that; but do not introduce into his religion what is not part of it.

It is therefore obligatory upon the students of knowledge to explain to the people and to say to them: occupy yourselves with the legislated, correct acts of worship: remember Allah, pray upon the Prophet at all times, establish prayer, give zakat, be good to the Muslims at all times. As for making a particular festival in the year—and Allah did not make in the year except three festivals only: the festival of Adha, the festival of Fitr, and the weekly festival, which is Friday—as for introducing other festivals, you are introducing into the religion of Allah what He did not legislate.

Then Allah, blessed and exalted, said: "Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds; for them is a reward never to be cut off." "For them is a reward" means: a recompense. "Never to be cut off" means: not interrupted, but continuous forever and ever. The verses concerning the everlasting nature of Paradise are numerous and well known in the Book and the Sunnah, and they are not so difficult that we need to cite them to you now, since they are clear, and praise be to Allah.

The reward of the Hereafter never ends, unlike the world, where there is a time when trees bear fruit and a time when they do not, or a time when the earth produces and a time when it does not. No; the reward there is permanent: "And for them is their provision therein, morning and evening." [Maryam 62].

We ask Allah, the Exalted, to make us and you among the believers who do righteous deeds and avoid evil deeds; indeed He is Generous and Bountiful. And may Allah's blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad and upon his family and all his companions.
